title: Sell Mineral Rights in Crabtree, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Crabtree, PA | Westmoreland County
metaDescription: Crabtree sits near Greensburg in Westmoreland County's Marcellus footprint. We buy PA mineral and royalty interests directly from owners, cash offer, no broker.
heroLead: Crabtree sits just outside Greensburg, close enough to the Westmoreland County seat that most families here recorded their original deeds at the same courthouse their grandparents did.
intro: Crabtree isn't its own municipality, it's a small community within a larger township, which means the mineral history here is tied closely to what's happened across Westmoreland County more broadly. Operators like EQT and CNX have held acreage across this county for years, and while Crabtree itself may not have a well pad on every corner, nearby units have shaped what many families' interests are actually worth.
If you've got a Crabtree-area mineral interest sitting untouched in a filing cabinet, or a royalty check you don't fully understand, we're glad to look at it and make a direct cash offer.

sections.heading: A Community Within a Larger Drilling Picture
paragraphs: Because Crabtree isn't incorporated on its own, its mineral activity is really a question about the surrounding township's leasing and permitting history. We pull that data specifically for your parcel rather than speaking in generalities about Westmoreland County as a whole, since activity can vary block by block even within a single township.
This matters more than it might seem. Two neighboring farms can have very different mineral value depending on which side of a unit boundary they happen to fall on.

sections.heading: Old Farm Deeds Near Greensburg
paragraphs: A lot of Crabtree-area land has stayed in the same families for generations, farms that predate any oil and gas leasing entirely. When Marcellus leasing arrived, these families often signed their first-ever mineral lease, sometimes with terms that were more favorable to the operator than what's become standard since. If your family's lease is from that early wave, it's worth having someone look at the actual terms rather than assuming they're current market standard.
We review these older leases as part of evaluating any interest, since the lease terms directly affect what a royalty or mineral sale is worth.

sections.heading: Selling Without Disrupting the Farm
paragraphs: For families still actively farming near Crabtree, selling mineral rights while keeping the land itself intact is usually the goal, not selling the farm, just the interest underground. That separation is exactly what a mineral rights sale allows. Your surface ownership, your fields, your operation, none of that changes.

faqs.question: Crabtree isn't its own town. Does that affect my mineral rights?
faqs.answer: No, ownership is tied to the recorded deed and township, not whether Crabtree has its own municipal government. We check the specific township's activity for your parcel.

faqs.question: My family's lease is from the early Marcellus leasing wave. Could the terms be outdated?
faqs.answer: It's possible. Early leases sometimes had terms less favorable to owners than what became standard later. We review the actual lease before making an offer.

faqs.question: Will selling mineral rights affect our ability to keep farming?
faqs.answer: No. Mineral and surface rights are separate. Selling your minerals doesn't change your ownership or use of the farmland above them.
